title: slug_dupe.py's first call deepens a fresh clone to 14 days in one fetch (49 s), so runs timed out and skipped the duplicate check
problem: Since P083 slug_dupe.py refreshes origin/main with fetch_ref --days 14 in one fetch. In a fresh shallow cloud clone that deepen dominates the call, and runs that gave the command 60 s lost the refresh and the check. P083's own refresh test sat inside the `if __name__ == "__main__":` block and never ran.
evidence: python3 platform/ci/friction_rank.py --live --ungated --days 3, 2026-11-25: cluster 19, 2 sessions, 'Timed out (>60 s) refreshing origin/main in the shallow clone'
time python3 platform/ci/slug_dupe.py pnpm in this session's fresh clone: 49.4 s (919 -> 4,325 commits); a repeat call 6.4 s
python3 -m unittest -v test_slug_dupe on main: test_refreshes_stale_origin_main_first not listed (defined under the main guard)
change: Fetch the tip first (fetch_ref days=0: only commits newer than the held history), then deepen to --days under --budget seconds (default 30, fetch_ref gains timeout=); on expiry print the window actually searched. Move the dead test into the class; check_uncollected_tests.py flags tests under the main guard in every tracked test file.
metric: Run-record doc_friction entries naming slug_dupe.py with 'timed out' or 'timeout', per 7 days after merge; and wall time of a first slug_dupe.py call in a fresh cloud clone
source: friction_rank.py cluster on platform/ci/slug_dupe.py (2026-11-25) and this run's timing
